takeaway: Auer rods on bone marrow are almost diagnostic of acute myeloid leukaemia. Owl eye nuclei mean CMV; Reed-Sternberg cells mean Hodgkin lymphoma.

question.text: A 65-year-old man has fatigue, mouth ulcers, marked hepatosplenomegaly and neck and supraclavicular masses. Which bone marrow result would practically confirm the diagnosis?

lines.text: Tiredness, mouth ulcers, a huge liver and spleen, and neck lumps: acute myeloid leukaemia.
Masses in the neck and supraclavicular fossa fit too.
Now look inside the blast cell on the marrow aspirate.
Auer rods, thin red needles, are almost diagnostic of the condition.
The median age at diagnosis is sixty-five, and it is more common in men.
Owl eye nuclei mean cytomegalovirus. Reed-Sternberg cells mean Hodgkin lymphoma, usually diagnosed on lymph node biopsy.
So the answer is Auer rods.
